macro.reasoning: The engine is at cycle 84 with 50 cycles of history. In the CMAPSS FD001 dataset, engines typically fail between cycles 125-250. The sensor readings show stable nominal values with occasional deviations but no sustained degradation trend. Key sensors (2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 20, 21) remain within normal operating ranges. The RUL at cycle 84 for a typical FD001 engine with this profile is approximately 41 cycles (total life ~125 cycles).

micro.reasoning: The engine is at cycle 84 with 50 cycles of history. Sensor deviations show intermittent anomalies (sensors 17, 8, 12, 15, 4, 21) but no sustained degradation trend. In NASA C-MAPSS FD001, engines typically fail around 125-250 cycles. With 84 cycles elapsed and capped RUL at 125, remaining life is approximately 125 - 84 = 41 cycles.

synthesis.reasoning: Both macro and micro forecasts converge on 41 cycles. The engine is at cycle 84; in the FD001 dataset, healthy engines reach the capped RUL of 125 cycles, so remaining life ≈ 125 − 84 = 41. Sensor readings show only intermittent, non-sustained deviations (e.g., sensors 17, 8, 12, 15, 4, 21) with no clear degradation trend, supporting the nominal 41-cycle estimate. Uncertainty is low given the consistent operating regime and dataset-typical total life.
